title: [Switch 2, SUBS, NSO] Super Mario Sunshine added to Nintendo Switch Online Expansion Pack @ Nintendo Switch Online
body:
Deal: [Switch 2, SUBS, NSO] Super Mario Sunshine added to Nintendo Switch Online Expansion Pack @ Nintendo Switch Online

[A 1] I've been waiting for this one, great game.
Time to break out the GC Controller and see how well those L R triggers work.
[SoulButter] Extremely satisfying refilling FLUDD with the GC controller.
[PainToad] https://retrododo.com/super-mario-sunshine-now-runs-natively…
[mett139] Give it to me straight, doc, why this and not a classic emulator?
[corgi-runner] That version is a recomp. A recomp is a process that takes compiled code from old console games (like N64, PS1, or Xbox 360) and translates it into native code for modern computers. Basically like a native port of the OG game for modern PCs.
There are dozens / hundreds of these recomps out there now. Some of the more well-known ones are The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Ship of Harkinian) and Star Fox 64 (lots of 64 games) and the recent Pokemon Red and Blue recomps where the devs got the OG 2D game running in 3D and even first-person lol.
[mett139] Thanks for the rundown. I just saw that Pokemon recomp the other day and figured there was more to it all. Sounds like smoother performance than emulators and more than what people do with cheat codes and rom hacks?
[belongsinforums] And now vr mods with motion controls for breath of the wild and oot
[LuthLexor] Way better performance. An emulator is doing a lot of overhead, using a lot of compute to interpret the rom file as the original hardware would.
Often these recomps have quality of life improvements built in too.
[Erwark] Yeah, the quality of life is big factor. Run at native resolution, widescreen aspect ratio, often the camera is overhauled for early 3D era (when they were still figuring it out).
eg. Zelda Ocarina/Majora allow for free aim camera (not just z-targeting to re-centre). You can bind extra item slots to the dpad and all sorts of little tweaks to address choices that maybe didn't age well. It's all your choice, too. Something like the Twilight Princess port, Dusklight, added all these settings as a native-looking in game menu.
[Altashi] It's really strange how they haven't yet added Colosseum, despite having the sequel on there already.
[Darkvolcos] Because Nintendo love doing things that don't make sense. Sucks they focused on this rather than a game that hadn't already been ported.
[mett139] Makes sense now why 'Super Mario 3D All-Stars' was axed and replaced with 'Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2'.
[xmagic] It was a Mario 35 anniversary limited release so was only available for a year or so. Just like the SMB35 game which I wished to last longer. It's quite a bit fun to play battle royale style. While galaxy 1+2 is a normal game release. It's not going anywhere.
Though games in all-stars are enhanced emulation, galaxy 1+2 are actually ports. Both will feel a bit different from playing NSO Classics.
[hawktalk] Super Mario Bros 35 was a great game (and like Tetris 99 - one I constantly finished first in haha).
[TheDukeOfNukem] It's a hot take, but it's right.
I don't really like Galaxy either tbh, but leaps and bounds above Sunshine.
[theSav] Sunshine is such a polarising game haha. Good to see that’s alive and well here!
I completed Sunshine & can’t argue that FLUDD is a cool mechanic. But that pachinko machine… And the whacky out-of-control janky controls.. 🤮 no please.
Somehow I still haven’t managed to finish Galaxy yet
[hawktalk] I'm not a fan of ANY 3D Mario.
Give me 2D Mario or give me death!
